title: Resolve sporadic scheduler pause causing long-context backlog and multi-tenant queue starvation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers on Dedicated and Hosted reported intermittent 5-20x tail latency spikes for long-context requests during mixed-length traffic bursts. This ticket tracks investigation, hotfix, tests, and rollout to stop sporadic scheduler pauses that allow short requests to flood admission, causing KV cache eviction and starvation of long-context flows.

Background: Over the past two weeks we've received 3 escalations (SE-924, SE-931, SE-940) from high-throughput customers. Symptoms: long-context generation requests (>=8k tokens) queue up behind a sudden microburst of short requests; after ~30-90s the scheduler appears to 'pause' batching for long-context lanes causing backlog amplification and elevated P95/P99 for those customers.

Observed impact: Dedicated pools see SLO violations (latency > 2x target) and error rate increases from client-side timeouts. Hosted tenants occasionally hit throttles due to congestion. Root cause hypothesis: a transient race between the admission controller's burst detector and the batching scheduler's prefetch/resume handshake. When burst detector triggers an aggressive small-request admission window, the resume handshake for long-context admission path can be skipped due to an edge-case mutex ordering, resulting in scheduler threads spinning on an empty admission queue for long-context batches while short requests saturate kernels and cause KV eviction.

Goal: implement deterministic resume handshake, add defensive backoff when admission windows oscillate, and add integration tests that reproduce mixed-length microbursts. Deliver a targeted hotfix for affected Dedicated pools and a staged rollout for Hosted.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.24 with current scheduler to staging cluster with two tenants (tenant-A long-context-heavy, tenant-B short-request-heavy).
2) Ramp tenant-A baseline steady traffic of long-context requests (avg 6-10k tokens) to warm KV caches.
3) Inject a 10s microburst from tenant-B of small (<20 token) requests at 10-20x baseline QPS.
4) Observe admission controller logs: look for burst_detector events and scheduler resume/handshake logs. Monitor p99 latency for tenant-A and KV cache eviction rate.
5) Reproduce in a loop until the scheduler pause manifests (~1-10 iterations in our staging runs).
mitigation_and_hotfix: 1) Hotpatch: add a short jittered backoff (50-200ms) before giving up on resume handshake to avoid transient skip (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342).
2) Temporary config knob: reduce aggressive_burst_threshold for affected Dedicated pools to avoid admission oscillation for 48 hours while we roll full fix.
3) Communication: customer success notified impacted customers and applied pool-level guardrails; support playbook created (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/SE-924-response).
engineering_notes: Investigation logs: scheduler thread dump and admission traces attached to internal S3: s3://redwood-internal/incidents/2026-03-scheduler-pause/

Root cause: race in AdmissionController::maybe_resume() where _resume_flag cleared by burst_detector path before scheduler thread reads it. The critical section was protected by different mutexes leading to a TOCTOU. Fixed by centralizing resume flag under admission_lock and adding state machine transitions (see PR).

We observed increased KV churn: eviction rate spiked by 3x during replayed microbursts, contributing to degraded long-context render times. Fix avoids unnecessary eviction by preserving long-context reservations during transient bursts.

Edge-case: if a tenant's tokens-per-second drops sharply while admission window is open, we must not starve long-context lanes. Added unit tests and a golden harness for mixed-length traffic (tests added in runtime/tests/scheduler_mixed_burst_test.cc).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic reproduce in staging before fix and no scheduler pause after fix under same reproduction steps.
P95/P99 for long-context flows in dedicated-staging return to baseline (within 10% of pre-burst numbers) across 5 repeated microburst runs.
Hotfix validated by dogfooding on two affected Dedicated pools for 48h with no SLO regressions for other tenants.
Code review approvals from Runtime and Infra (at least 2 reviewers) and CI green on all scheduler and integration tests.
Release notes and runbook updated; postmortem link added to ticket.
test_plan: Unit tests for AdmissionController state transitions and resume handshake (new tests in runtime/unit).
Stress test in staging with fault-injection of microbursts and KV cache pressure to capture eviction metrics and scheduler traces.
Chaos test: random mutex reorder fuzzing to ensure no TOCTOU regressions.
Load test on a small Dedicated cluster mirror using customer-like traffic traces from SE-924 (redacted).
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: apply hotpatch to 2 canary Dedicated pools (non-prod customer mirrors) and monitor for 6 hours. Metrics: p99 latency, KV eviction rate, scheduler resume events. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/ops/scheduler-resume?orgId=1
2) If stable, push full runtime-1.24 patch to remaining Dedicated pools during low-traffic windows with 15m pause points between rings.
3) Hosted: staged rollout across regions with feature flag gated resume-state-machine true/false. Roll back quickly if anomalies.
4) Post-rollout validate SLOs for 72h and mark ticket Done after postmortem and runbook updates.
